title: Export and import settings
body:
I run two Detent installs side by side (the release and a local build) and wanted the same setup in both. There is no way to move it: the setup lives in app-private SharedPreferences, so I read each setup page and copied it by hand.

`android:allowBackup="true"` covers Google's device restore, but not moving a setup between installs or builds, or after a reset without a Google backup.

An idea: export and import rows on the feel page that write and read one small JSON file through the system file picker (`ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT` / `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT`), with:

- layout, theme, side
- dial apps, quick apps, recent
- sound, haptics, dots, lock screen, Detent bar, voice, web search

Import would skip apps that are not installed and themes that do not exist.

Related: `Prefs` saves the theme as an index into `THEMES`. A new theme added in the middle of the list (the omarchy themes are alphabetical) shifts every saved theme after it, so after an update some people would wake up on a different theme. Saving the theme name next to the index would fix that, and an export file would need the name anyway.

PRs are off here, so if you want either part I can put it on a branch in my fork for you to pull or copy.

title: Theme colours from outside the app, and a theme that keeps the live wallpaper
body:
On my desktop (Hyprland, with colours from pywal) the palette follows the wallpaper, and I wanted the dial to match it and to keep my live wallpaper (Wallpaper Engine) behind the dial.

Two things get in the way today:

1. Colours come only from the built-in `THEMES` list.
2. Every theme paints over the system wallpaper (`windowShowWallpaper` is false and the background is opaque). With "lock screen" on, Detent also replaces the system wallpaper with its own image, so a live wallpaper is lost.

I have this working on a branch in my fork: https://github.com/kvnloo/detent/tree/feat/hyprland-colors. It adds one theme whose bg, fg and accent come from a broadcast and are saved in prefs:

```
adb shell am broadcast -a app.detent.launcher.SET_COLORS \
  -n app.detent.launcher/.ColorsReceiver --es bg 181f23 --es fg d1deda --es accent c8be72
```

That theme draws only its shade over the system wallpaper (`FLAG_SHOW_WALLPAPER` and a transparent window), and never calls `setWallpaper`. A watcher on my desktop sends the new colours whenever the wallpaper changes.

Open questions:

- Should the receiver be guarded by a permission? As written, any app on the phone can recolour the theme.
- Is "show the system wallpaper" better as its own toggle that works with any theme, rather than tied to this one theme?

PRs are off here, so if this fits Detent, take whatever is useful from the branch. I can reshape it to whatever you prefer.

title: [Feature] Add theme-aware Android app widget support to the home screen
body:
### Problem
Currently I have to leave the launcher to check information that I would normally want available at a glance, such as weather, daily steps, activity progress, or other health information. It would be great to have a small, customisable widget area that complements the existing clock and dial without compromising the minimal aesthetic.

### Proposed feature

Introduce support for hosting Android app widgets directly on the Detent home screen.

Ideally, users should be able to add widgets from applications installed on their devices, such as:

- **Weather:** Current temperature, conditions, and forecast.
- **Health:** Daily steps, activity progress, sleep summaries, etc. (for example, Samsung Health widgets).
- **Other widgets:** Clock, calendar, battery, or other standard Android app widgets.

Rather than implementing integrations for every individual application, Detent could support the standard Android App Widget framework, allowing users to select widgets from compatible installed applications.

### Placement and layout

The widget area should integrate naturally with the existing clock/readout.

Some possible placement options:

- Beside the clock/readout, where screen dimensions permit.
- Below the clock/readout, forming a compact vertical widget stack.
- An adaptive arrangement depending on the selected dial layout and available screen space.

It would also be nice to let users choose which widgets appear and remove them without having to reset their launcher configuration.

### Theme integration

This is particularly important to me. The widgets should feel like part of Detent rather than externally embedded components.

Ideally:

- Widget containers should inherit the currently selected Detent theme.
- Backgrounds, surfaces, borders, and surrounding UI should use the theme's colour palette.
- Widget dimensions and spacing should adapt to the selected layout.
- Theme changes should be reflected without requiring the user to re-add widgets.
- Where supported by Android and the widget provider, Detent should communicate the appropriate theme colours so widgets can adapt their own appearance.

For third party widgets whose internal appearance cannot be controlled by the host, a theme aware container would still help maintain visual consistency.

### Suggested implementation

Since Detent is built using Jetpack Compose, this could be explored through Android's standard `AppWidgetHost`, `AppWidgetManager`, and `AppWidgetHostView` APIs.

The implementation should also support widget configuration activities, persistent widget IDs, and proper cleanup when widgets are removed.

title: [Security]: add SHA-256 verification for the Gradle Wrapper distributio
body:
### Description

The repository's `gradle-wrapper.properties` specifies a Gradle distribution URL and enables URL validation, but does not configure `distributionSha256Sum`. Without this property, the Gradle Wrapper does not verify the SHA-256 checksum of the downloaded Gradle distribution. Although the distribution is downloaded over HTTPS, checksum verification provides an additional integrity check against a compromised download or targeted man-in-the-middle attack.

### Proposed improvement

Add the official SHA-256 checksum corresponding to the configured Gradle distribution.

For example:

```properties
distributionUrl=https\://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-9.3.1-bin.zip
distributionSha256Sum=<official-sha256-checksum>
```

The checksum should be obtained from Gradle's official release checksum reference rather than generated from an unverified local download.

### References

- https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/gradle_wrapper.html
- https://gradle.org/release-checksums/

The repository currently does not allow opening PRs. You can either allow a pull or implement this from your side.

title: Would you welcome patches for app renaming and search?
body:
I’ve been enjoying Detent and have prepared three changes I’d like to contribute:

- Rename apps from the dial menu or by holding a search result. Custom names stay lowercase, can be reset, and are used for search and alphabetical ordering.
- Open an app automatically when typing in app search leaves exactly one match. Web search and the quick app picker still require an explicit choice.
- Return to the dial when Android sends a Home action with the app drawer open, even if the window has lost focus. This also removes the app drawer’s redundant cancel button.

The patch applies to `a86a67e`. The release build and all 48 tests passed, and lint reported no errors.

I noticed pull requests are turned off for this repository. Would any of these changes be useful, and if so, how would you prefer I share them? I’m happy to split the patches for review.
